svg.title: Two strip directions give the same geometric area
svg.desc: The region between y equals x squared and y equals two x lies in the first quadrant, between intersections zero,zero and two,four. A vertical strip has height two x minus x squared, integrated with respect to x from zero to two. A horizontal strip has width square root y minus y over two, integrated with respect to y from zero to four. Both give area four thirds. The positive square root branch is used because this region has nonnegative x. Orange strips show representative boundary differences and their integration variables.
